When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat on the pulpit, he would call the adhan at the door of the mosque; when he descended, he would establish the prayer. Then Abu Bakr did likewise, and 'Umar likewise, until 'Uthman's time, when the people increased and the dwellings spread apart, so he added a first adhan and ordered the first call to be made from a house he had in the market called al-Zawra'; he would be called to from it. When 'Uthman sat on the pulpit, his first muezzin would call the adhan, and when he descended, he would establish the prayer. This was not criticized against him.

The common reading is al-Jumu'ah with a damma on the mim; al-A'mash read it with a light pronunciation and a sukun on the mim. Both are dialects, and its plural is jum'ah and jum'at.

Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us, saying: I heard al-Kisa'i report from Sulayman, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: The Qur'an was revealed with the heavy (tathqil) and the emphatic (tafkhim) [pronunciation]. Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayd said: The light form (takhfif) is good and it is [........] [[An unreadable word.]] in the school of Arabic, like ghurfah and ghurf, tarfah and tarf, hujrah and hujr. Al-Farra' said: There is also a third dialect: jum'ah with a fatha, as you say rajul dahkah and hamazah and lumazah; it is the dialect of the Banu 'Uqayl. It is said: it is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ). This day was named jum'ah because

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-'Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn Abi Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Abi Umayyah narrated to us, saying: Qays al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from Qurtha' al-Dabbi, from Sulayman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It was only named jum'ah because Adam gathered his creation on it."
[291] [[The beginning of the hadith is in Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/709, no. 21039; the continuation is not present.]] It is also said: because Allah, glory be to Him, finished creating things on it, so the created beings came together in it.

It is said: because it gathers the congregations in it; it is said: because people gather for the prayer on it; it is said: the first to name it jum'ah was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hafsawayh narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Hafs al-Hulwani narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from his father, from Abu Salamah, who said: The first to say "amma ba'd" was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, and he was the first to name the jum'ah "jum'ah." It used to be said of the jum'ah: al-'Arubah. It is also said: the first to name it jum'ah were the Ansar.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: The people of Medina gathered before the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina and before the Friday prayer was revealed, and they were the ones who named it jum'ah. The Ansar said: "The Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, and the Christians have a day likewise. Come, let us make a day on which we gather, remember Allah, glory and majesty be to Him, pray, and give thanks to Him," or as they said.

They said: "Saturday is for the Jews and Sunday for the Christians; so make it the day of 'Arubah." They used to call the day of Friday the day of 'Arubah. They gathered at As'ad ibn Zurarah, and he led them in two rak'ahs that day and reminded them. So they named it the day of Friday when they gathered to him. As'ad ibn Zurarah slaughtered a sheep for them, and they ate their midday and evening meals from one sheep, because of their small number. Then Allah, glory be to Him, revealed concerning that, after ﴿When the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday﴾ the verse. This was the first Friday congregation held in Islam.

As for the first Friday congregation the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held with his companions:

The people of biography and history said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived as an emigrant and stopped at Quba' with the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, on Monday, twelve nights past the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the forenoon had grown bright. He (ﷺ) remained at Quba' on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and founded their mosque. Then he went out among them on Friday, intending Medina, and the Friday prayer overtook him in the Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, in the bottom of a valley belonging to them, where a mosque had been made on that day at that place. This was the first Friday.

And al-Hasan said: It is recommended and not obligatory.

Sa'id said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held it in Islam; he gave a sermon in this Friday, and it is said it was the first sermon he gave in Medina. He (ﷺ) said: "All praise is due to Allah. I praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, seek His guidance, and believe in Him and do not disbelieve in Him, and I take as enemy whoever disbelieves in Him. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and light and admonition, during a gap between the messengers, with scarcity of knowledge, with the straying of people, with the cessation of time, with the nearness of the Hour and the approach of the term. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has erred, gone astray, and strayed far. I enjoin you to the fear of Allah, for it is the best that a Muslim can enjoin upon a Muslim: that he urge him toward the Hereafter and command him to the fear of Allah. So beware of what Allah has warned you of concerning Himself. Indeed, fear of Allah for one who acts upon it with dread and apprehension of his Lord is a help and a truthfulness toward what you seek of the affair of the Hereafter. Whoever sets right what is between him and Allah in his affair, secretly and openly, intending nothing but the face of Allah, will have a remembrance for him in his immediate affair and a store for what follows death, when a man will be in need of what he has sent forward; and whatever evil there is, he will wish that between it and him were a far distance. ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants.﴾ The one whose speech is true and whose promise is fulfilled, there is no changing of it, for He says: ﴿The word is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants.﴾ Be mindful of Allah in your immediate and final affairs, secretly and openly, for whoever is mindful of Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and magnify his reward ﴿and whoever fears Allah has certainly achieved a great attainment.﴾ Indeed, fear of Allah protects from His hatred, protects from His punishment, and protects from His wrath. Indeed, fear of Allah whitens faces, pleases the Lord, and raises the rank. Take your share and do not neglect what is due to Allah, for Allah has taught you His Book and made clear to you His way, so that He may know those who are truthful and know the liars. So do good as Allah has done good to you, take as enemy His enemies, ﴿and strive for Allah with the striving due to Him.﴾ He has chosen you and named you 'the Muslims,' so that whoever perished might perish with clear evidence and whoever lives might live with clear evidence. There is no might and no power except through Allah. Remember Allah much, and work for what comes after this day, for whoever sets right what is between him and Allah, Allah will suffice him for what is between him and the people. That is because Allah judges over people, and they cannot judge over Him; He possesses people, and they do not possess Him. Allah is greatest; there is no might and no power except through the Mighty Allah."[292] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/115; Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/11.]]

Therefore the khutbah became a condition for the validity of the Friday prayer, and this is the view of the majority of scholars. Al-Hasan said: it is recommended and not obligatory. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is in the position of the two rak'ahs of Zuhr; so if one leaves it and performs the Friday prayer, one has performed the two rak'ahs of Zuhr. The least that suffices of the khutbah is to praise Allah, send blessings upon His Prophet, enjoin the fear of Allah, the Exalted, and recite a verse of the Qur'an in the first khutbah; and in the second, four [things] are obligatory as in the first, except that the obligatory element replaces the recitation of a verse with supplication. This is the view of most scholars and jurists. Abu Hanifah said: if one suffices with praising God, or glorifying (tasbih), or saying Allahu akbar, it is sufficient. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: the obligatory element is what falls under the name khutbah.

Then standing is a condition for the validity of the khutbah, when one is able to stand, according to the view of the general body of jurists, except Abu Hanifah, who did not make it a condition for it. The evidence that standing is a condition for the khutbah is His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And they left you standing.﴾

And the hadith of Ibn 'Umar: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never gave two khutbahs except while standing."

Al-Shafi'i has two opinions on purity during the khutbah: in the new (al-jadid) view he said it is a condition for the khutbah; in the old (al-qadim) view he said it is not a condition, and this is the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him.

This is the explanation of the first Friday congregation held in Islam, and the first Friday congregation the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held, and the first khutbah he gave in it in Medina. As for the first Friday congregation held after it in Medina, Ibn 'Abbas said: the first Friday congregation held in Islam after the Friday in Medina was in a village called Juwatha, from the villages of Bahrain.

His saying: ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾ means: go to it and act for it.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Handhalah narrated to us, saying: I heard Salim say: Ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah" [then proceed to the remembrance of Allah].

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz, with others, informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: al-Shafi'i informed us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: I never heard 'Umar recite it except as "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah."

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kalmawani informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Hafs narrated to us, saying: al-Sari ibn Khuzaymah narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hanzhalah, from Salim, from 'Umar, that he used to recite it "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah." Al-A'mash narrated from Ibrahim, who said: 'Abd Allah used to recite it "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah," and he would say: "If it were recited fas'aw, I would have run until my cloak fell off." This is also the reading of Abu al-'Aliyah. Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, it is not walking on foot; they were only forbidden to come to the prayer except with tranquility and dignity, but [the striving is] with the hearts, the intention, and humility."

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab informed us, saying: Sa'id was asked about the virtue of Friday, and he informed us from Qatadah that he used to say concerning this verse, ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾: the striving (al-sa'y) is that you strive with your heart and your deeds, and it is walking to it. He said: he used to interpret this verse, ﴿And when he reached with him the striving﴾ [[Surah al-Saffat: 102.]] as "when he walked with him." Al-Kalbi said: "when he did his deed like his deed."

Muhammad ibn Hamdawayh informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' informed us, saying: al-Shafi'i said: The striving in this place is the action. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾ [[Surah al-Layl: 4.]] and He said, glory be to Him: ﴿And that man will have only what he strove for﴾ [[Surah al-Najm: 39.]] and He, exalted, said: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 205.]] Zuhayr said: "People strove after them so that they might overtake them, but they did not overtake them, nor meet them, nor fall short in reaching the remembrance of Allah," meaning the prayer.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab concerning ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾: "the admonition of the imam." ﴿And leave trade﴾ means sale and purchase, because bay' (sale) encompasses both meanings together, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not separated,"[293] [[Kitab al-Musnad li-l-Shafi'i: 138; Musnad Ahmad: 2/9.]] meaning the seller and the buyer. Al-Akhtal said:

"He sold his sons, some of them, for a worthless thing, and I sold al-'Ala' of Dhubyan for Malik."[[Al-Sihah: 2/645; Lisan al-'Arab: 4/240; in the sources it is attributed to al-Hutay'ah, not al-Akhtal.]]

He means by the first the selling and by the last the buying. Trade is forbidden at the second adhan. Al-Zuhri said: at the emergence of the imam. Al-Dahhak said: when the sun has passed its zenith, buying and selling are forbidden. Al-Suddi related from Abu Malik: some people used to sit in the cemetery of al-Zubayr and buy and sell when the call to prayer for Friday was made, and they did not stand up; so this verse was revealed.

﴿That is better for you than trade, if you know﴾: that which I mentioned, namely attending the Friday prayer, listening to the Friday sermon, and performing the obligation, is better for you than trading, if you know the benefits of yourselves and their harms.

Mention of that verse:

Know that the Friday prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim except five persons: women, children, slaves, travelers, and the sick. What indicates this is what:

Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Azhari [in Isfara'in] informed us, saying: Abu 'Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz informed us, saying: al-Muzani informed us, saying: al-Shafi'i said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Salamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hutami narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he heard a man from the Banu Wa'il say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Friday prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim except a woman, a child, or a slave."[294] [[Kitab al-Musnad li-l-Shafi'i: 61.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Hibri narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Salamah al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mathna Salman ibn Yazid al-Ka'bi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Trade is forbidden at the adhan on Friday, and speech is forbidden during the khutbah, and trade becomes lawful after the Friday prayer. The Friday prayer is not obligatory upon four: the sick, the slave, the child, and the woman. Whoever goes to it for amusement or trade, Allah will be free of him, and Allah is Self-sufficient, Praiseworthy."[295]

The Friday prayer is obligatory upon the people of villages when they hear the call from the city (al-misr). The time for considering the hearing of the adhan is when the muezzin is loud, the voices are calm, and the wind is still, and the muezzin's standing place is at the wall of the town; each village is measured by the wall nearest to it. This is the position of al-Shafi'i. Ibn 'Umar, Abu Hurayrah, and Anas said: the Friday prayer is obligatory upon one who is within ten miles of the city. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: it is obligatory upon one whom lodging there sustains. Al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon one within six miles. Rabi'ah: four miles. Malik and al-Layth: three miles.

Abu Hanifah said: the Friday prayer is not obligatory upon the people of the countryside (al-sawad), whether the village is near the town or far, to the point that it is related that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan was asked whether the Friday prayer is obligatory upon the people of his dwellings, between which and Kufa there was a river channel, and he said: No.

The jurists differed about the number of people by whom the Friday prayer is validly constituted. Al-Hasan said: it is validly constituted by two. Al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Abu Yusuf said: by three. Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu Hanifah said: by four. Rabi'ah said: by twelve, in the opinion. Al-Shafi'i said: the Friday prayer is not validly constituted by fewer than forty persons. He said: every village in which forty adult, sane, free, resident men gather, who do not leave it in winter or summer except for a necessary journey, the Friday prayer is obligatory upon them. Malik said: if a village has a market and a mosque, the Friday prayer is obligatory upon them without regard to number. Abu Hanifah said: the Friday prayer is not obligatory upon the people of the countryside and villages, and it is not lawful for them to establish it there; and he stipulated for the obligation and validity of the Friday prayer: a city (misr) with a congregational mosque, a ruling authority that prevails, a standing market, and a flowing river. He argued

with the hadith of 'Ali, may Allah honor his face: "There is no Friday prayer and no market except in a congregational city (misr jami')," and in some reports: "except for the people of a congregational city." Some have declared it weak.

The proof for Abu Hanifa is the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first Friday prayer held after the Friday prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ) in Medina was in a village in the region of Bahrain called Juwatha." It is also narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to the people of Bahrain: "Pray the Friday prayer wherever you are." The Friday prayer is valid to hold without the permission or presence of the ruler (sultan). Abu Hanifa said: one of its conditions is the Imam or his deputy.

The proof that the ruler is not a condition for the validity of the Friday prayer is what is reported: al-Walid ibn ʿUqba, the governor of Kufa, was late one day in attending the Friday prayer, so ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud advanced and led the people in the Friday prayer without his permission.

It is also reported that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, led the people in the Friday prayer on the day ʿUthman was besieged, and it is not transmitted that he sought his permission. And it is reported that when Saʿid ibn al-ʿAs, the governor of Medina, was expelled from Medina, Abu Musa al-Ashʿari led the people in the Friday prayer without seeking permission.

It is not permissible to pray more than one Friday prayer in one city; if it is prayed a second time, it is invalid. Abu Yusuf said: if the city has two sides, it is permissible for each side to hold a Friday prayer. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: it is permissible to hold two Friday prayers in one city, by way of istihsan (juristic preference).

As for the threat directed at one who abandons the Friday prayer without an excuse:

Abu ʿAmr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Ahmar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Hakam informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed us, from Usayd ibn Usayd al-Baqqad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Qatada, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever abandons the Friday prayer three times without necessity, Allah will seal his heart." [296] [[al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 1/292.]]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik narrated from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Let people cease who hear the call on Friday and then do not attend it; otherwise Allah will seal their hearts, or they will surely be among the heedless, or they will surely be among the people of the Fire." [297] [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin of al-Tabarani: 2/285, no. 1352.]]

It is also narrated that he (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said: "Allah has made the Friday prayer obligatory upon you in this place of mine, on this day of mine, [in this month of mine, of this year of mine, until the Day of Resurrection]. Whoever abandons it during my lifetime or after my death, while having a just or unjust ruler, without an excuse, Allah will not bless him, nor gather his affairs. Beware, he has no Hajj, beware, he has no fast. But whoever repents, Allah will accept his repentance." [298] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/343; Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 7/721, no. 21092.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Fathuwi informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Qati'i related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Hasan ibn ʿAli related to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hurr, from Maymun ibn Abi al-Musayyab, who said: "I wanted to attend the Friday prayer in the time of al-Hajjaj. I prepared to go, then I said: 'Where am I going? To pray behind this man?' Once I said: 'I will go,' and once I said: 'I will not go.' I settled my mind on going, and a caller called to me from the side of the house: 'O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah' [Qur'an 62:9]. I was sitting writing a letter, and something occurred to me: if I wrote it, my letter would be adorned, and I would have lied; if I removed it, there would be some ugliness in my letter, and I would have spoken the truth. I said once: 'Write,' and once: 'Do not write.' I settled my mind on leaving it, and I left it. Then a caller called to me from the side of the house: 'Allah keeps firm those who have believed with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter' [Qur'an 14:27]."

As for the reward of one who attends the Friday prayer:

Ahmad ibn Abi informed us, along with others, saying: Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb related to us, saying: ʿIsa ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Baqiyya related to us, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Hamza related to me, from Abu Nadra, from Abu Raja' al-ʿAttar, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and ʿUmar ibn Husayn, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday, his sins and errors will be expiated. When he sets out walking [to the Friday prayer], for every step a deed of twenty years is written for him. When he has finished [in the source: departed] from the [Friday] [in the source: prayer], he is rewarded with the deed of two hundred years." [299]

Ahmad ibn Abi informed us, along with others, who said: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm related to us, saying: al-Rabiʿ informed us, saying: al-Shafiʿi informed us, saying: Malik informed us, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday with the bath of janabah, then goes, it is as if he offered a camel. Whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he offered a cow. Whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he offered a ram. Whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he offered a hen. Whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he offered an egg. When the Imam comes out, the angels are present, listening to the remembrance." [300] [[Kitab al-Musnad of al-Shafiʿi: 62.]]

Abu ʿAmr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Basri informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shawdhab related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Daqiqi related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken up to the heaven, I saw beneath the Throne seventy cities, each city like this world of yours seventy times, filled with angels glorifying Allah and sanctifying Him, and in their glorification they say: 'O Allah, forgive whoever attended the Friday prayer; O Allah, forgive whoever bathed on Friday.'" [301] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/119.]]

As for the virtue of the day of Friday:

Abu ʿAmr al-Furati, Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Hafiz, Abu Muhammad al-Kinani and Abu ʿAli al-Thawri informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: al-Rabiʿ informed us, saying: al-Shafiʿi informed us, saying: Malik informed us, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sihad, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best day on which the sun has risen is the day of Friday: on it Adam was created, on it he was made to descend, on it [he was forgiven] and on it he died, and on it the Hour will be established. There is no creature except that it glorifies Allah on Friday from the time of morning until sunrise, out of fear of the Hour, except jinn and humans. And there is an hour on it in which no Muslim servant meets it while asking Allah for something except that He gives it to him." [302] »

Abu Hurayra said: Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "It is the last hour of the day of Friday." I said to him: "How can it be the last hour, when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: no Muslim servant meets it while he is praying, and that hour is not one in which one prays?" Ibn Salam said: "Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not say: 'Whoever sits in a place waiting for the prayer, he is in prayer until he prays'?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then that is it." [303] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/451.]]

ʿAbd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Hind informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to us, saying: Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid al-Sakuni related to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Khaythama related to us, from ʿUthman ibn Abi Muslim, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was delayed with us one day; when he came out we said: "Were you detained?" He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me in the form of a white woman with a black spot, and said: 'This Friday holds good for you and your community, and it was desired by the Jews and Christians, but they missed it.' I said: 'O Jibril, what is this black spot?' He said: 'This is the hour on Friday; no Muslim who meets it asks Allah for good except that He gives it to him, or stores up for him the like of it on the Day of Resurrection, or turns away from him the like of evil. It is the best of days with Allah. The people of Paradise call it the day of al-Marnad.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the day of al-Marnad?' He said: 'In Paradise there is a valley whose plant has the scent of white musk. Allah, glorified and exalted, descends every Friday and places His Chair there. Then pulpits of light are brought and placed behind it, and the angels surround them. Then a chair of gold is brought and placed. Then the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the believers who dwell in the chambers come and sit. Then Allah, glorified and exalted, swears and says: "O My servants, ask." They say: "We ask Your good pleasure." He says: "I have been pleased with you, so ask." They ask what they wish, and Allah gives them what they wish and multiples it, giving them what no eye has seen and no heart of a human has conceived. Then He says: "Did I not fulfil My promise to you and complete My favour upon you? This is the place of My honour." Then they return to their chambers and come back every Friday.' I said: 'O Jibril, what are their chambers?' He said: 'Of white pearl, or red ruby, or green emerald, their doors separated from them, with their spouses in them, and with rivers flowing through them.'"

ʿAbd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn ʿAbd al-Jalil mentioned, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ghalib al-Basri al-Zahid related to us, after having said: Dinar, the freedman of Anas ibn Malik, related to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The night of Friday and the day of Friday are twenty-four hours; for Allah, glorified, in every hour there are six hundred thousand men freed from the Fire." [304] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/201, with variation.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 62, verse 8–9 (part 1 of 2):

Say: "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do." ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave trade.﴾ [The phrase] "on the day of Friday" means "on the day of Friday," like His saying, ﴿Or have they a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book...﴾ [[Surah Fatir: 40.]] meaning "in the earth." By this call is meant the adhan (call to prayer) when the imam sits on the pulpit for the khutbah (sermon). What indicates this is what:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Khalid al-Wahbi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had one muezzin, Bilal, and he had no other muezzin besides him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat on the pulpit, he would call the adhan at the door of the mosque; when he descended, he would establish the prayer. Then Abu Bakr did likewise, and 'Umar likewise, until 'Uthman's time, when the people increased and the dwellings spread apart, so he added a first adhan and ordered the first call to be made from a house he had in the market called al-Zawra'; he would be called to from it. When 'Uthman sat on the pulpit, his first muezzin would call the adhan, and when he descended, he would establish the prayer. This was not criticized against him.

The common reading is al-Jumu'ah with a damma on the mim; al-A'mash read it with a light pronunciation and a sukun on the mim. Both are dialects, and its plural is jum'ah and jum'at.

Muhammad ibn Na'im informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us, saying: I heard al-Kisa'i report from Sulayman, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: The Qur'an was revealed with the heavy (tathqil) and the emphatic (tafkhim) [pronunciation]. Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayd said: The light form (takhfif) is good and it is [........] [[An unreadable word.]] in the school of Arabic, like ghurfah and ghurf, tarfah and tarf, hujrah and hujr. Al-Farra' said: There is also a third dialect: jum'ah with a fatha, as you say rajul dahkah and hamazah and lumazah; it is the dialect of the Banu 'Uqayl. It is said: it is the dialect of the Prophet (ﷺ). This day was named jum'ah because

Al-Hasan informed us, saying: al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Makhlad al-'Attar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn Abi Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Abi Umayyah narrated to us, saying: Qays al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from Qurtha' al-Dabbi, from Sulayman, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It was only named jum'ah because Adam gathered his creation on it."
[291] [[The beginning of the hadith is in Kanz al-'Ummal: 7/709, no. 21039; the continuation is not present.]] It is also said: because Allah, glory be to Him, finished creating things on it, so the created beings came together in it.

It is said: because it gathers the congregations in it; it is said: because people gather for the prayer on it; it is said: the first to name it jum'ah was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Hafsawayh narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Hafs al-Hulwani narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, from his father, from Abu Salamah, who said: The first to say "amma ba'd" was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy, and he was the first to name the jum'ah "jum'ah." It used to be said of the jum'ah: al-'Arubah. It is also said: the first to name it jum'ah were the Ansar.

Al-Husayn informed me, saying: Ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: The people of Medina gathered before the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina and before the Friday prayer was revealed, and they were the ones who named it jum'ah. The Ansar said: "The Jews have a day on which they gather every seven days, and the Christians have a day likewise. Come, let us make a day on which we gather, remember Allah, glory and majesty be to Him, pray, and give thanks to Him," or as they said.

They said: "Saturday is for the Jews and Sunday for the Christians; so make it the day of 'Arubah." They used to call the day of Friday the day of 'Arubah. They gathered at As'ad ibn Zurarah, and he led them in two rak'ahs that day and reminded them. So they named it the day of Friday when they gathered to him. As'ad ibn Zurarah slaughtered a sheep for them, and they ate their midday and evening meals from one sheep, because of their small number. Then Allah, glory be to Him, revealed concerning that, after ﴿When the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday﴾ the verse. This was the first Friday congregation held in Islam.

As for the first Friday congregation the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held with his companions:

The people of biography and history said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived as an emigrant and stopped at Quba' with the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, on Monday, twelve nights past the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, when the forenoon had grown bright. He (ﷺ) remained at Quba' on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and founded their mosque. Then he went out among them on Friday, intending Medina, and the Friday prayer overtook him in the Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, in the bottom of a valley belonging to them, where a mosque had been made on that day at that place. This was the first Friday.

And al-Hasan said: It is recommended and not obligatory.

Sa'id said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held it in Islam; he gave a sermon in this Friday, and it is said it was the first sermon he gave in Medina. He (ﷺ) said: "All praise is due to Allah. I praise Him, seek His help, seek His forgiveness, seek His guidance, and believe in Him and do not disbelieve in Him, and I take as enemy whoever disbelieves in Him. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, whom He sent with guidance and light and admonition, during a gap between the messengers, with scarcity of knowledge, with the straying of people, with the cessation of time, with the nearness of the Hour and the approach of the term. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has erred, gone astray, and strayed far. I enjoin you to the fear of Allah, for it is the best that a Muslim can enjoin upon a Muslim: that he urge him toward the Hereafter and command him to the fear of Allah. So beware of what Allah has warned you of concerning Himself. Indeed, fear of Allah for one who acts upon it with dread and apprehension of his Lord is a help and a truthfulness toward what you seek of the affair of the Hereafter. Whoever sets right what is between him and Allah in his affair, secretly and openly, intending nothing but the face of Allah, will have a remembrance for him in his immediate affair and a store for what follows death, when a man will be in need of what he has sent forward; and whatever evil there is, he will wish that between it and him were a far distance. ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants.﴾ The one whose speech is true and whose promise is fulfilled, there is no changing of it, for He says: ﴿The word is not changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants.﴾ Be mindful of Allah in your immediate and final affairs, secretly and openly, for whoever is mindful of Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and magnify his reward ﴿and whoever fears Allah has certainly achieved a great attainment.﴾ Indeed, fear of Allah protects from His hatred, protects from His punishment, and protects from His wrath. Indeed, fear of Allah whitens faces, pleases the Lord, and raises the rank. Take your share and do not neglect what is due to Allah, for Allah has taught you His Book and made clear to you His way, so that He may know those who are truthful and know the liars. So do good as Allah has done good to you, take as enemy His enemies, ﴿and strive for Allah with the striving due to Him.﴾ He has chosen you and named you 'the Muslims,' so that whoever perished might perish with clear evidence and whoever lives might live with clear evidence. There is no might and no power except through Allah. Remember Allah much, and work for what comes after this day, for whoever sets right what is between him and Allah, Allah will suffice him for what is between him and the people. That is because Allah judges over people, and they cannot judge over Him; He possesses people, and they do not possess Him. Allah is greatest; there is no might and no power except through the Mighty Allah."[292] [[Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/115; Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/11.]]

Therefore the khutbah became a condition for the validity of the Friday prayer, and this is the view of the majority of scholars. Al-Hasan said: it is recommended and not obligatory. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is in the position of the two rak'ahs of Zuhr; so if one leaves it and performs the Friday prayer, one has performed the two rak'ahs of Zuhr. The least that suffices of the khutbah is to praise Allah, send blessings upon His Prophet, enjoin the fear of Allah, the Exalted, and recite a verse of the Qur'an in the first khutbah; and in the second, four [things] are obligatory as in the first, except that the obligatory element replaces the recitation of a verse with supplication. This is the view of most scholars and jurists. Abu Hanifah said: if one suffices with praising God, or glorifying (tasbih), or saying Allahu akbar, it is sufficient. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: the obligatory element is what falls under the name khutbah.

Then standing is a condition for the validity of the khutbah, when one is able to stand, according to the view of the general body of jurists, except Abu Hanifah, who did not make it a condition for it. The evidence that standing is a condition for the khutbah is His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿And they left you standing.﴾

And the hadith of Ibn 'Umar: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never gave two khutbahs except while standing."

Al-Shafi'i has two opinions on purity during the khutbah: in the new (al-jadid) view he said it is a condition for the khutbah; in the old (al-qadim) view he said it is not a condition, and this is the view of Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him.

This is the explanation of the first Friday congregation held in Islam, and the first Friday congregation the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held, and the first khutbah he gave in it in Medina. As for the first Friday congregation held after it in Medina, Ibn 'Abbas said: the first Friday congregation held in Islam after the Friday in Medina was in a village called Juwatha, from the villages of Bahrain.

His saying: ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾ means: go to it and act for it.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Makki informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Handhalah narrated to us, saying: I heard Salim say: Ibn 'Umar said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah" [then proceed to the remembrance of Allah].

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz, with others, informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: al-Shafi'i informed us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, who said: I never heard 'Umar recite it except as "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah."

Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kalmawani informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Hafs narrated to us, saying: al-Sari ibn Khuzaymah narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hanzhalah, from Salim, from 'Umar, that he used to recite it "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah." Al-A'mash narrated from Ibrahim, who said: 'Abd Allah used to recite it "fa-mdu ila dhikr Allah," and he would say: "If it were recited fas'aw, I would have run until my cloak fell off." This is also the reading of Abu al-'Aliyah. Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, it is not walking on foot; they were only forbidden to come to the prayer except with tranquility and dignity, but [the striving is] with the hearts, the intention, and humility."

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab informed us, saying: Sa'id was asked about the virtue of Friday, and he informed us from Qatadah that he used to say concerning this verse, ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾: the striving (al-sa'y) is that you strive with your heart and your deeds, and it is walking to it. He said: he used to interpret this verse, ﴿And when he reached with him the striving﴾ [[Surah al-Saffat: 102.]] as "when he walked with him." Al-Kalbi said: "when he did his deed like his deed."

Muhammad ibn Hamdawayh informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' informed us, saying: al-Shafi'i said: The striving in this place is the action. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾ [[Surah al-Layl: 4.]] and He said, glory be to Him: ﴿And that man will have only what he strove for﴾ [[Surah al-Najm: 39.]] and He, exalted, said: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 205.]] Zuhayr said: "People strove after them so that they might overtake them, but they did not overtake them, nor meet them, nor fall short in reaching the remembrance of Allah," meaning the prayer.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, saying: 'Ali ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab concerning ﴿then proceed to the remembrance of Allah﴾: "the admonition of the imam." ﴿And leave trade﴾ means sale and purchase, because bay' (sale) encompasses both meanings together, and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The two parties to a sale have the option as long as they have not separated,"[293] [[Kitab al-Musnad li-l-Shafi'i: 138; Musnad Ahmad: 2/9.]] meaning the seller and the buyer. Al-Akhtal said:

"He sold his sons, some of them, for a worthless thing, and I sold al-'Ala' of Dhubyan for Malik."[[Al-Sihah: 2/645; Lisan al-'Arab: 4/240; in the sources it is attributed to al-Hutay'ah, not al-Akhtal.]]

He means by the first the selling and by the last the buying. Trade is forbidden at the second adhan. Al-Zuhri said: at the emergence of the imam. Al-Dahhak said: when the sun has passed its zenith, buying and selling are forbidden. Al-Suddi related from Abu Malik: some people used to sit in the cemetery of al-Zubayr and buy and sell when the call to prayer for Friday was made, and they did not stand up; so this verse was revealed.

﴿That is better for you than trade, if you know﴾: that which I mentioned, namely attending the Friday prayer, listening to the Friday sermon, and performing the obligation, is better for you than trading, if you know the benefits of yourselves and their harms.

Mention of that verse:

Know that the Friday prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim except five persons: women, children, slaves, travelers, and the sick. What indicates this is what:

Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Azhari [in Isfara'in] informed us, saying: Abu 'Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz informed us, saying: al-Muzani informed us, saying: al-Shafi'i said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Salamah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hutami narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he heard a man from the Banu Wa'il say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Friday prayer is obligatory upon every Muslim except a woman, a child, or a slave."[294] [[Kitab al-Musnad li-l-Shafi'i: 61.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman al-Hibri narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn Salamah al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mathna Salman ibn Yazid al-Ka'bi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Trade is forbidden at the adhan on Friday, and speech is forbidden during the khutbah, and trade becomes lawful after the Friday prayer. The Friday prayer is not obligatory upon four: the sick, the slave, the child, and the woman. Whoever goes to it for amusement or trade, Allah will be free of him, and Allah is Self-sufficient, Praiseworthy."[295]

The Friday prayer is obligatory upon the people of villages when they hear the call from the city (al-misr). The time for considering the hearing of the adhan is when the muezzin is loud, the voices are calm, and the wind is still, and the muezzin's standing place is at the wall of the town; each village is measured by the wall nearest to it. This is the position of al-Shafi'i. Ibn 'Umar, Abu Hurayrah, and Anas said: the Friday prayer is obligatory upon one who is within ten miles of the city. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: it is obligatory upon one whom lodging there sustains. Al-Zuhri said: it is obligatory upon one within six miles. Rabi'ah: four miles. Malik and al-Layth: three miles.

Abu Hanifah said: the Friday prayer is not obligatory upon the people of the countryside (al-sawad), whether the village is near the town or far, to the point that it is related that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan was asked whether the Friday prayer is obligatory upon the people of his dwellings, between which and Kufa there was a river channel, and he said: No.

The jurists differed about the number of people by whom the Friday prayer is validly constituted. Al-Hasan said: it is validly constituted by two. Al-Layth ibn Sa'd and Abu Yusuf said: by three. Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu Hanifah said: by four. Rabi'ah said: by twelve, in the opinion. Al-Shafi'i said: the Friday prayer is not validly constituted by fewer than forty persons. He said: every village in which forty adult, sane, free, resident men gather, who do not leave it in winter or summer except for a necessary journey, the Friday prayer is obligatory upon them. Malik said: if a village has a market and a mosque, the Friday prayer is obligatory upon them without regard to number. Abu Hanifah said: the Friday prayer is not obligatory upon the people of the countryside and villages, and it is not lawful for them to establish it there; and he stipulated for the obligation and validity of the Friday prayer: a city (misr) with a congregational mosque, a ruling authority that prevails, a standing market, and a flowing river. He argued

with the hadith of 'Ali, may Allah honor his face: "There is no Friday prayer and no market except in a congregational city (misr jami')," and in some reports: "except for the people of a congregational city." Some have declared it weak.

The proof for Abu Hanifa is the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: "The first Friday prayer held after the Friday prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ) in Medina was in a village in the region of Bahrain called Juwatha." It is also narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to the people of Bahrain: "Pray the Friday prayer wherever you are." The Friday prayer is valid to hold without the permission or presence of the ruler (sultan). Abu Hanifa said: one of its conditions is the Imam or his deputy.

The proof that the ruler is not a condition for the validity of the Friday prayer is what is reported: al-Walid ibn ʿUqba, the governor of Kufa, was late one day in attending the Friday prayer, so ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud advanced and led the people in the Friday prayer without his permission.

It is also reported that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, led the people in the Friday prayer on the day ʿUthman was besieged, and it is not transmitted that he sought his permission. And it is reported that when Saʿid ibn al-ʿAs, the governor of Medina, was expelled from Medina, Abu Musa al-Ashʿari led the people in the Friday prayer without seeking permission.

It is not permissible to pray more than one Friday prayer in one city; if it is prayed a second time, it is invalid. Abu Yusuf said: if the city has two sides, it is permissible for each side to hold a Friday prayer. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: it is permissible to hold two Friday prayers in one city, by way of istihsan (juristic preference).

As for the threat directed at one who abandons the Friday prayer without an excuse:

Abu ʿAmr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Ahmar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Hakam informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b informed us, from Usayd ibn Usayd al-Baqqad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Qatada, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever abandons the Friday prayer three times without necessity, Allah will seal his heart." [296] [[al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 1/292.]]

ʿAbd Allah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik narrated from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Let people cease who hear the call on Friday and then do not attend it; otherwise Allah will seal their hearts, or they will surely be among the heedless, or they will surely be among the people of the Fire." [297] [[Musnad al-Shamiyyin of al-Tabarani: 2/285, no. 1352.]]

It is also narrated that he (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said: "Allah has made the Friday prayer obligatory upon you in this place of mine, on this day of mine, [in this month of mine, of this year of mine, until the Day of Resurrection]. Whoever abandons it during my lifetime or after my death, while having a just or unjust ruler, without an excuse, Allah will not bless him, nor gather his affairs. Beware, he has no Hajj, beware, he has no fast. But whoever repents, Allah will accept his repentance." [298] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 1/343; Kanz al-ʿUmmal: 7/721, no. 21092.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Fathuwi informed us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Qati'i related to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Hasan ibn ʿAli related to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Hurr, from Maymun ibn Abi al-Musayyab, who said: "I wanted to attend the Friday prayer in the time of al-Hajjaj. I prepared to go, then I said: 'Where am I going? To pray behind this man?' Once I said: 'I will go,' and once I said: 'I will not go.' I settled my mind on going, and a caller called to me from the side of the house: 'O you who have believed, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, then hasten to the remembrance of Allah' [Qur'an 62:9]. I was sitting writing a letter, and something occurred to me: if I wrote it, my letter would be adorned, and I would have lied; if I removed it, there would be some ugliness in my letter, and I would have spoken the truth. I said once: 'Write,' and once: 'Do not write.' I settled my mind on leaving it, and I left it. Then a caller called to me from the side of the house: 'Allah keeps firm those who have believed with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter' [Qur'an 14:27]."

As for the reward of one who attends the Friday prayer:

Ahmad ibn Abi informed us, along with others, saying: Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb related to us, saying: ʿIsa ibn Ahmad related to us, saying: Baqiyya related to us, saying: al-Dahhak ibn Hamza related to me, from Abu Nadra, from Abu Raja' al-ʿAttar, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and ʿUmar ibn Husayn, who both said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday, his sins and errors will be expiated. When he sets out walking [to the Friday prayer], for every step a deed of twenty years is written for him. When he has finished [in the source: departed] from the [Friday] [in the source: prayer], he is rewarded with the deed of two hundred years." [299]

Ahmad ibn Abi informed us, along with others, who said: Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm related to us, saying: al-Rabiʿ informed us, saying: al-Shafiʿi informed us, saying: Malik informed us, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday with the bath of janabah, then goes, it is as if he offered a camel. Whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he offered a cow. Whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he offered a ram. Whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he offered a hen. Whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he offered an egg. When the Imam comes out, the angels are present, listening to the remembrance." [300] [[Kitab al-Musnad of al-Shafiʿi: 62.]]

Abu ʿAmr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Basri informed us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shawdhab related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik al-Daqiqi related to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken up to the heaven, I saw beneath the Throne seventy cities, each city like this world of yours seventy times, filled with angels glorifying Allah and sanctifying Him, and in their glorification they say: 'O Allah, forgive whoever attended the Friday prayer; O Allah, forgive whoever bathed on Friday.'" [301] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/119.]]

As for the virtue of the day of Friday:

Abu ʿAmr al-Furati, Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Hafiz, Abu Muhammad al-Kinani and Abu ʿAli al-Thawri informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Yaʿqub ibn Yusuf related to us, saying: al-Rabiʿ informed us, saying: al-Shafiʿi informed us, saying: Malik informed us, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sihad, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best day on which the sun has risen is the day of Friday: on it Adam was created, on it he was made to descend, on it [he was forgiven] and on it he died, and on it the Hour will be established. There is no creature except that it glorifies Allah on Friday from the time of morning until sunrise, out of fear of the Hour, except jinn and humans. And there is an hour on it in which no Muslim servant meets it while asking Allah for something except that He gives it to him." [302] »

Abu Hurayra said: Abd Allah ibn Salam said: "It is the last hour of the day of Friday." I said to him: "How can it be the last hour, when the Prophet (ﷺ) said: no Muslim servant meets it while he is praying, and that hour is not one in which one prays?" Ibn Salam said: "Did the Prophet (ﷺ) not say: 'Whoever sits in a place waiting for the prayer, he is in prayer until he prays'?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then that is it." [303] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/451.]]

ʿAbd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Ibn Hind informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to us, saying: Abu Badr Shuja' ibn al-Walid al-Sakuni related to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Khaythama related to us, from ʿUthman ibn Abi Muslim, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was delayed with us one day; when he came out we said: "Were you detained?" He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me in the form of a white woman with a black spot, and said: 'This Friday holds good for you and your community, and it was desired by the Jews and Christians, but they missed it.' I said: 'O Jibril, what is this black spot?' He said: 'This is the hour on Friday; no Muslim who meets it asks Allah for good except that He gives it to him, or stores up for him the like of it on the Day of Resurrection, or turns away from him the like of evil. It is the best of days with Allah. The people of Paradise call it the day of al-Marnad.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the day of al-Marnad?' He said: 'In Paradise there is a valley whose plant has the scent of white musk. Allah, glorified and exalted, descends every Friday and places His Chair there. Then pulpits of light are brought and placed behind it, and the angels surround them. Then a chair of gold is brought and placed. Then the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the believers who dwell in the chambers come and sit. Then Allah, glorified and exalted, swears and says: "O My servants, ask." They say: "We ask Your good pleasure." He says: "I have been pleased with you, so ask." They ask what they wish, and Allah gives them what they wish and multiples it, giving them what no eye has seen and no heart of a human has conceived. Then He says: "Did I not fulfil My promise to you and complete My favour upon you? This is the place of My honour." Then they return to their chambers and come back every Friday.' I said: 'O Jibril, what are their chambers?' He said: 'Of white pearl, or red ruby, or green emerald, their doors separated from them, with their spouses in them, and with rivers flowing through them.'"

ʿAbd al-Khaliq informed us, saying: Abu al-ʿAbbas ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn ʿAbd al-Jalil mentioned, saying: Abu Muhammad Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ghalib al-Basri al-Zahid related to us, after having said: Dinar, the freedman of Anas ibn Malik, related to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The night of Friday and the day of Friday are twenty-four hours; for Allah, glorified, in every hour there are six hundred thousand men freed from the Fire." [304] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 6/201, with variation.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 62, verse 10–11:

﴿فَإِذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ﴾ means: when it has been finished, i.e., when he has completed it.

﴿فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ means: disperse throughout the land, for trade and for managing your needs.

﴿وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ means: seek of Allah's bounty, i.e., provision. These two imperatives express permission and choice, like His saying, ﴿وَإِذا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطادُوا﴾ [[Surat al-Ma'idah: 2.]].

ʿAqil has reported that Abu al-Farah informed them from Abu Ja'far al-Tabari, who said: "al-ʿAbbas ibn Abi Talib related to me, who said: ʿAli ibn al-Mu'afa ibn Ya'qub al-Mawsili related to us, who said: Abu ʿAli al-Da'i related to us, from Abu Khalaf, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the words of Allah, ﴿فَإِذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾: 'It is not the seeking of worldly gain, but visiting a sick person, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother for the sake of Allah.'" [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/14.]]

al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Makhul said: ﴿وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ is the seeking of knowledge.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said: ﴿فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ refers to Saturday.

﴿وَإِذا رَأَوْا تِجارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً﴾ — the verse.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, who said: ʿAli ibn Harb related to us, who said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, who said: Husayn related to us, from Salim ibn al-Ja'd, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: A caravan arrived while we were praying the Friday prayer with the Prophet (ﷺ), so the people rushed out toward it, and only twelve men remained, including myself. Then the verse ﴿وَإِذا رَأَوْا تِجارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً﴾ was revealed.

al-Hasan and Abu Malik said: The people of Madinah were struck by hunger and high prices. Dihyah ibn Khalifah arrived with a shipment of oil from al-Sham while the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the Friday sermon. When they saw it, they rose toward him at al-Baqi', fearing they would be beaten to it, and only a small group remained with the Prophet (ﷺ), among them Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. Then this verse was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, had you followed one another until none of you remained, the valley would have flowed with fire upon you." [305] [[Musnad Abi Ya'la: 3/468.]]

The two Muqatils said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering the Friday sermon, Dihyah ibn Khalifah ibn Furwah al-Kalbi, then one of the Banu al-Khazraj, then one of the Banu Zayd ibn Manat ibn ʿAmir, arrived from al-Sham with merchandise. Whenever he arrived, no unmarried woman in Madinah remained without coming to him, and he would bring everything they needed, such as flour, wheat or other goods. He would stop at the Ahjar al-Zayt, a place in the market of Madinah, and then beat a drum to announce his arrival, so people would come out to him. One Friday he arrived, and this was before he had accepted Islam, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit delivering the sermon. The people went out, and only twelve men and a woman remained in the mosque. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for these, stones would have been rained down upon them from the sky." [306] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/11.]] And Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse.

Ibn ʿAbbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: Only eight men remained in the mosque. Ibn Kaysan said: They went out, except for eleven men and a woman.

Qatadah and Muqatil said: We have been told that they did this three times, and each time a caravan came from al-Sham, and all of this coincided with Friday.

Mujahid said: They used to rise toward their water-carrying camels and their travel, following trade and amusement, so Allah, the Exalted, revealed ﴿وَإِذا رَأَوْا تِجارَةً أَوْ لَهْواً﴾. The exegetes said: it means the drum, because when the caravan came to Madinah, they would greet it with drums and whistling.

Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah said: When the slave girls were married, they would pass by with flutes and drums, and the people rushed out toward them, so this verse was revealed. His words ﴿انْفَضُّوا إِلَيْها﴾ return the pronoun to trade, because it is more important and superior. This question has already passed.

Talhah ibn Musarrif read: "وإذا رأوا لهوا أو تجارة انفضّوا إليها" (and when they saw amusement or trade, they rushed toward it).

﴿وَتَرَكُوكَ قائِماً﴾ — standing on the pulpit.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, who said: Abu ʿAmr ibn al-Hasan informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Sa'id related to us, who said: My father related to us, who said: Husayn related to us, from Mis'ar and Abu Hanifah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, from Hassan, from ʿUbaydah, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allah, that he was asked: Did the Prophet (ﷺ) deliver the sermon standing or sitting?

He said: Do you not read, ﴿وَتَرَكُوكَ قائِماً﴾?

﴿قُلْ ما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ مِنَ اللَّهْوِ وَمِنَ التِّجارَةِ﴾ — Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi read: "خير من اللهو والتجارة للذين آمنوا" (better than amusement and trade for those who believe).

﴿وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ﴾ because He is the originator of provisions; so to Him alone ask, and from Him alone seek.
